The assertion is checking that the result of the XPath "//location[2]/preceding::node()[3]" is the text node of employeeCount, but it is actually the address node. This suggests there might be an issue with how the "preceding" axis is being resolved in the DOM model representation by JXPath.

From the covered classes and methods, the likely relevant class is org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer, which is used to represent nodes and paths in the DOM. Within this class, methods related to node traversal and comparison, such as compareChildNodePointers, getRelativePositionByName, childIterator, and testNode, might be involved in determining node order and axis navigation.

To further understand how the preceding axis nodes are selected and ordered, I will review the code for the method childIterator in org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer, as it seems relevant to iterating over child nodes which could be used for axis navigation.
